ledger.x: 1893: Britain declares a protectorate over the southern Solomon Islands (June 1893).
1897: Bellona, Rennell and Sikaiana 'were added to the Protectorate in 1897'.
1898: the Santa Cruz group and the Reef Islands are added.

1900: Choiseul, Ysabel, Shortland and Fauro join the protectorate: they 'were transferred to the United Kingdom under the Samoa Tripartite Convention of 1899'; 'In October 1900, the High Commissioner issued a Proclamation extending the Protectorate to the islands in…

1942: the Japanese invade the Solomon Islands (January 1942): 'after the Japanese invasion of the Solomon Islands in January 1942'; the Guadalcanal campaign page: they 'had occupied Tulagi in May 1942'.
1942: the Guadalcanal campaign: 'On 7 August 1942, Allied forces, predominantly U.S.
1943: the Guadalcanal campaign ends: 'It was fought between 7 August 1942 and 9 February 1943'; the Japanese 'evacuated their last forces by 9 February 1943'.
1978: the Solomon Islands become independent on 7 July 1978.

wars.name: Guadalcanal campaign
wars.outcome: Allied landings on 7 August 1942; the Japanese 'evacuated their last forces by 9 February 1943'.

certainty.note: The protectorate's limits are 'the southern Solomon Islands'; the line with the German islands (Choiseul, Ysabel, Shortland, Fauro) is not on the page and the islands are named, not bounded.
Fixed by the Tripartite Convention (14 November 1899) and the October 1900 Proclamation; an island group whose border is the sea and the Bougainville Strait.
